info.title: CaseForge Generator
info.description:
Generator turns one authoritative Vault Engagement Record into an in-memory
case-study draft in English, German or Turkish. It never reads a source corpus, a
seed file or a PDF at request time, and it never trusts facts supplied in a request
body: `POST /generate` takes a record id and fetches the record from Vault itself.

Every language, English included, is produced through the configured model, so
`OPENAI_API_KEY` is required for all three. The model may only rewrite visible prose:
source ids, references, missing-data markers, quantities, technologies and naming
consent are re-checked afterwards, and a violation is an HTTP error rather than a
successful draft.

Generating a draft is not approval. Submit the final edited draft to Verifier, obtain
human approval, then publish through Publisher's independent final gate.

`GET /health` reports liveness only. It proves nothing about Vault, Librarian or the
model provider. See `docs/CF-123-runbook.md` for setup, dependencies, timeouts and
troubleshooting.

get.description: Returns a fixed body without contacting Vault, Librarian or the model provider. A green health check does not mean a draft can be generated.

post.summary: Generate a draft from one Vault record
post.description:
Reads `GET {VAULT_URL}/engagements/{record_id}`, builds the grounded draft and returns it in the requested language.

`language` defaults to `en`; unknown fields are rejected. English is not a shortcut: it is produced through the same model step as German and Turkish, so the provider must be configured for every language.

`page` and `page_ref` carry the **source record id**, not a PDF page number.

post.summary: Generate an English draft from a submitted record body
post.description:
Only the `id` field of the submitted body is used. Every fact comes from Vault, so a modified body cannot change the generated content.

Deprecated. Use `POST /generate` with `{record_id, language}`. This adapter is kept for existing callers and reads its facts from Vault like every other route.

post.summary: Generate an English draft from a submitted record body
post.description:
Identical to `POST /generator/mcs`. Only the body's `id` is used; the facts come from Vault.

Deprecated. Use `POST /generate` with `{record_id, language}`. This adapter is kept for existing callers and reads its facts from Vault like every other route.

post.summary: Select one record through Librarian, then generate
post.description:
`query` and `language` are **query-string parameters**, not a JSON body. Librarian's `POST /match` picks a single engagement id with `top_k=1`, and that record is then read from Vault as usual.

This route is the only one that depends on Librarian: generating from a record id you already know works while Librarian is down.

Deprecated. Use `POST /generate` with `{record_id, language}`. This adapter is kept for existing callers and reads its facts from Vault like every other route.

McsDraft.title: McsDraft
McsDraft.description: Canonical single-source draft. Every title, section entry and citation is bound to one Vault record, and only this prose may be rendered. The whole document is limited to 24000 serialised characters and 32 levels of nesting.

engagement_ids.description: Exactly `[record_id]`; a draft never spans two sources.

sections.description: The five standard case-study sections, always all present.

context.description: Client type and region, composed from the source record.

technology.description: Technologies recorded on the source, joined into one entry.

outcomes.description: Measured outcomes, or a `[MISSING: ...]` marker when the source records none.

citations.description: One entry per recorded outcome; empty when the source records none.

client_named.description: True only when the source record sets `may_be_named` to true. It reports the source's consent; it does not grant it.

GeneratorHealth.title: GeneratorHealth
GeneratorHealth.description: Liveness only; no dependency is contacted to produce it.

BearerAuth.description: Optional service-to-service credential. This API never enforces a bearer token on its own endpoints. An incoming `Authorization` header is forwarded to Vault unchanged; when it is absent the configured `CASEFORGE_TOKEN` is sent instead. A rejected credential therefore surfaces as Vault's own 401 or 403, not as a local authentication failure.

CorrelationId.name: X-Correlation-ID
CorrelationId.description: Trace forwarded to every dependency and returned on handled responses. Any printable-ASCII value of at most 4096 characters is accepted; it does not have to be a UUID. Omit it to have one generated.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Validated under the same printable-ASCII and 4096-character rule as the other shared headers. This API neither deduplicates on it nor forwards it to Vault, so sending it guarantees no persistent deduplication.

BadHeader.description: A shared HTTP header was rejected before the route ran; the response still carries a generated trace. The limit is 4096 characters of printable ASCII (code points 32-126) on `X-Correlation-ID`, `Authorization` and `Idempotency-Key`.

X-Correlation-ID.description: The trace used for this request. A submitted value is preserved; a missing or empty one is replaced by a generated UUID. Requests the HTTP server rejects before the application sees them, and unhandled server errors, carry no trace.
